liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Turn On Your Love Light** (3 reviews): Band keeps drifting into psychedelic jamming while Pigpen keeps trying to pull them back to Lovelight; funny; Over-the-top Lovelight with a pandemonium-filled buildup to the ending, Bobby and Pig letting loose [11][12][17]
- **Dire Wolf** (2 reviews): Garcia and Weir sing nice harmonies on Dire Wolf; Reviewer's favorite Dire Wolf so far, with notable interplay between Garcia and Lesh [9][15]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer treasures their tape for its China Cat Sunflower, and says this soundboard version differs from it [13]
- **Me & My Uncle** (1 review): Weir sounds earnest and young on Me & My Uncle [9]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): This Black Peter wins the listener over with Garcia's slow drawling vocals and guitar, plus Phil's loping bass [10]
- **Cold Rain & Snow** (1 review): Cold Rain is mid-tempo with a striking vocal harmony, possibly involving Lesh, and sparse, straight-ahead instrumentation [9]
- Reviewer calls one version an all-time best, especially from 10:30 to 15:32 [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bobby's got a broken string**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.sirmick.89175.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 14 songs; 86 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.sirmick.89614.flac24**: soundboard; 14 songs; 86 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.miller.pitch-corrected.89862.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.miller.89281.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 84 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [5]
- **gd70-01-10.sbd.clugston.6663.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 87 min; rated 4.14/5 by 22 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording pretty clean, with very little hiss; Reviewer considers it a fine recording [12][15]

## Around the show

- Per DeadBase IX, this may be the complete show or only the last 86 minutes; China Cat as opener is uncertain [2]
- Reviewer sees the show as a good snapshot of the Dead's improvisational skill around 1970 [14]
- Typical of the era, the show leans on folk material, with early versions of Cold Rain and Snow and Black Peter [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.sirmick.89175.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: MR > R1 >RX (purported 2nd gen) [1]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.sirmick.89614.flac24**: transferred by SIRMick; source: MR > R1 > RX (purported to be 2nd gen) [2]. Also: A 16-bit streaming version of this source exists; uploader calls it the best source of the show [2]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.miller.pitch-corrected.89862.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe B Jones; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Reel-> Dat -> CD D [4]. Also: Source was mislabeled as a Master Reel; the Casey Jones intro is cut, but Casey Jones is pitch-corrected [4]
- **gd1970-01-10.sbd.miller.89281.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Reel-> Dat -> CD D [5]. Also: Source was mislabeled as a Master Reel, and the Casey Jones intro is cut [5]
- **gd70-01-10.sbd.clugston.6663.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Soundboard [6]. Also: Reviewer first heard the show on the Grateful Dead Hour about 15 years ago and taped it on cassette; Reviewer got a better copy around 1985 from Dave Grushkin; it differs from this soundboard version; Reviewer recorded the show in the late 1970s from WLIR radio, Long Island [6][12][13][17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Golden Hall - January 10, 1970](https://www.dead.net/show/january-10-1970) [27]
